newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch seal off area in bid to contain swine fever.
newsitem.headline: Dutch seal off area in bid to contain swine fever.

text.p: The Dutch Farm Ministry said on Saturday it had sealed off an area covering some 600 square kilometres in the south of the country in a bid to contain an outbreak of swine fever which has already spread to seven farms.

The transport of all manure and livestock, apart from poultry, has been banned inside the seclusion zone. The ministry has also designated a smaller area, within which around 30,000 pigs will be destroyed.
"This morning we found a seventh case in the same area as the others and a very large area has now been sealed off," a spokesman for the ministry told Reuters.
Dutch Agriculture Minister Jozias van Aartsen visited the region on Saturday to oversee the containment measures.

Swine fever, which last appeared in the Netherlands in 1992, is a highly contagious pig disease although it is not dangerous to humans. The latest outbreak was first discovered at a farm on Monday and more cases then came to light through the week.
The Netherlands exports around 750,000 tonnes of pigs and pork products every year and its trading partners are watching the situation closely.
On Friday, Poland closed its borders to all imports of Dutch pigs, pork and pork products and Belgium said it would tighten frontier checks, although stopped short of an outright ban.
The U.S. Agriculture Department said on Friday it was keeping a close eye on developments and would make a decision on what action it should take next week.
A USDA official said the Animal and Plant Heatlh Inspection Service was watching to see if the Dutch government was taking adequate measures to "successfully control the situation".
The outreak has so far been confined to a relatively small area in the province of North Brabant and the government hopes its seclusion policy will be sufficient to contain the disease.

The ban on the transport of animals covers an area that exceeds European Union disease management regulations which stipulate a transport embargo within a 10 kilometre radius of the centre of an outbreak, the farm ministry said.
"We're carrying out blood tests in the area. This is a very dangerous disease and it can spread very quickly, but we're hoping it has been contained," a spokeswoman said on Thursday.
The EU's Standing Veterinary Committee will hold a special meeting on Wednesday to discuss swine fever, focusing on the Netherlands and Germany, where there is also a serious outbreak.
Germany earlier this week prohibited the export of pigs for slaughter from four German states and ordered the destruction of over 14,000 pigs to try to contain it.
Belgium and Switzerland have already announced restrictions on imports from Germany of live pigs and pork meat.
